sugestoes.texto: The device-limit check and the subsequent insert/update are not atomic. Two concurrent anonymous auth requests with different device IDs can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert rows, causing the configured anonymous device limit to be exceeded. Wrap the count and write in a serializable transaction or use a single atomic upsert guarded by the limit to prevent the check-then-act race.

TagDevice is now invoked synchronously on the anonymous authentication hot path, so every cache-missed anonymous request blocks authentication on database I/O. The previous implementation ran tagging in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout; that safeguard is removed and auth latency now depends entirely on the request context. Keep tagging synchronous only for the limit-reached decision, or reintroduce a bounded timeout context to avoid hanging authentication when the database is slow.

The device-limit check and the subsequent insert/update are not atomic. Two concurrent anonymous requests with different device IDs can both see count < limit and both insert, so the actual device count can exceed the configured cap. Perform the count and the conditional insert/update inside a single transaction with serializable isolation, or enforce the cap at the database level.

TagDevice is now called synchronously inside Authenticate instead of in a background goroutine. Every anonymous authentication with a cache miss now blocks on a database insert/update before returning, increasing login latency and removing the previous 2-minute timeout boundary. Keep only the limit-check/enforcement on the hot path and move the tagging write back to an asynchronous call, or add a short explicit timeout.

The device limit is global and counts every distinct X-Grafana-Device-Id header value without per-client restrictions. Because the header is attacker-controlled and anonymous requests are unauthenticated, an attacker can cycle device IDs to exhaust the limit, causing CreateOrUpdateDevice to return ErrDeviceLimitReached and Authenticate to deny legitimate anonymous users. Add per-IP or per-session rate limiting before new devices are counted, or validate/bind the device identifier to the session.

ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 deviceLimit argument, but pkg/server/wire.go still registers it and binds anonstore.AnonStore without supplying that value. ProvideAnonymousDeviceService also no longer consumes anonstore.AnonStore, so the wire registration is stale and will break any injector that resolves the interface. Remove the anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and wire.Bind entries from pkg/server/wire.go, or revert to injecting the store via wire and add a provider for cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit.

The global `deviceLimit` counts every distinct header without per-client restrictions, so an attacker can cycle device IDs and exhaust the pool, making `CreateOrUpdateDevice` return `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and `Authenticate` deny legitimate users. Scope the count to `client_ip` and rate-limit new devices per IP or session.

`CountDevices` and the subsequent insert/update run outside a transaction, so concurrent anonymous requests can both see `count < s.deviceLimit` and insert past the cap. Wrap the check and write in a serializable transaction, or enforce the limit with a database constraint.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

sugestoes.texto: Create records legacy duration on Storage failure. When d.Storage.Create returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, so storage errors are mislabeled as legacy metrics and the storage duration histogram is never observed.

Delete discards the enriched logger and mislabels the success metric. ctx is reset with d.Log instead of log (line 97), dropping name/kind/method values, and the success path records name as the kind label (line 106) instead of options.Kind.

Update records legacy duration on Storage failure. When d.Storage.Update returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, so storage errors are reported against the wrong metric.

DeleteCollection's async legacy write records storage duration instead of legacy duration. The goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration for d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, so legacy operation latency/errors are mixed into the storage metric.

Update async legacy write no longer wraps objInfo with updateWrapper. The previous implementation and mode 2 pass an updateWrapper whose UpdatedObject returns the object already persisted to Storage; the new code passes the raw objInfo, causing Legacy.Update to recompute the object from its own old state and risking divergence between stores.

Every Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection spawns an unbounded goroutine with a 10-second timeout and no rate limiter or worker pool. Under high write load this creates unbounded goroutine and memory growth, and each goroutine may retain request-scoped values for up to 10 seconds.

Asynchronous legacy write failures in Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection are never logged; only the `is_error` metric label records the failure. This removes the error visibility that existed in the previous synchronous mode-3 implementation and in modes 1/2, making it hard to diagnose when the legacy safe-measure write fails.

Each async legacy write retains request-scoped values for ten seconds and can exhaust memory under heavy load because no rate limiter or worker pool bounds the goroutines. Cap the concurrency for `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection`.

issues.descricao: Delete puts the base d.Log instead of the enriched per-call logger into the context, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method fields.
issues.textoGolden: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

comentarios.texto: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` installs the mode-level logger instead of the request-scoped `log` built on line 96 (which carries name, kind and method) — a copy/paste error, as every other method in this file passes the composed `log`. Storage.Delete and the legacy delete goroutine therefore log without the per-request fields this PR is adding (and without the metrics method/kind context).
ctx is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of the enriched `log`. The delete logs then lose the name, kind and method values. Use `log`.
The Delete context uses d.Log rather than the per-call log. This is a logging-context inconsistency (not a data leak); use the per-call logger for consistency.

issues.descricao: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
issues.textoGolden: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

comentarios.texto: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

issues.descricao: Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

comentarios.texto: The Delete success-path metric passes `name` where every other call site in this file (lines 48, 103, 113, 156, 159) passes options.Kind in the kind/name argument slot. The storage-success sample for Delete is thus labelled with the object name instead of the resource kind, breaking label consistency with the other operations and with the error sample emitted at line 103. Use options.Kind here (or insert name consistently everywhere, matching the metric's label semantics).
recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) at line 106 passes the object name in the kind label slot.

recordStorageDuration is called with the object `name` as the `kind` label: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. Every other storage call site passes `options.Kind` (lines 73, 89, 103, 156, 159). This injects a per-object value into the kind label, corrupting the metric and giving it unbounded cardinality (one series per object name), which grows memory on every delete. Should be `options.Kind`.

issues.descricao: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

comentarios.texto: On a Storage.Create failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) — the failing subsystem is Storage, not Legacy, and it passes the storage start time. This records storage failures under the legacy metric, corrupting the dual-writer error dashboards (and contradicts the success path on line 48 which uses recordStorageDuration). Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

On a Storage.Update failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), attributing a storage failure and its storage duration to the legacy metric. This is inconsistent with the success path on line 132 (recordStorageDuration) and with mode1's semantics. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

The async goroutine performing the LEGACY DeleteCollection measures it with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Every other legacy write in this file uses recordLegacyDuration (lines 56, 113, 140); recording it under the storage metric reports legacy latency/errors as storage latency/errors. Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

issues.descricao: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

comentarios.texto: The async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns — which is immediately after Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return — so the goroutine's Legacy.Create can be canceled before completing, silently dropping the legacy write that this mode exists to guarantee. The same applies to the goroutines at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Detach the async context from request cancellation (e.g. derive from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background()) before applying the timeout.

The legacy write in Mode 3 became fire-and-forget, changing the contract callers relied on: previously Create (and, identically, Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) returned only after the LegacyStorage call had been made in-request; now it returns immediately and the write runs in a detached goroutine. Worse, the goroutine builds its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), which the API server cancels as soon as the handler returns/flushes the response — so the legacy write and its 10s timeout will typically be cancelled outright and the legacy store silently stops being updated, which is precisely what the new mode-3 integration cases assume still happens. Any detached work must be given a context not tied to the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a server-lifetime context), and consumers that depended on the synchronous legacy write need to be updated.

The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

issues.descricao: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.

comentarios.texto: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Restore forwarding of the committed result via updateWrapper instead of recomputing the update against legacy state.

issues.descricao: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

comentarios.texto: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

issues.descricao: The List error test case is still named 'not implemented' although List is now implemented and the case checks storage error propagation.

comentarios.texto: The test-case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" still describes the old stub List (which returned nil, nil with a "List not implemented" log). List is now implemented at dualwriter_mode3.go:79 and delegates to Storage.List; the case merely checks that a Storage error is propagated. The name contradicts the code it now exercises — rename it, e.g. "error when listing objects in the unified store fails".

issues.descricao: The Create test case name says 'only in the unified store' although Mode 3 also writes to legacy.

comentarios.texto: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

issues.descricao: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

comentarios.texto: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

issues.descricao: The storage-failure Create test registers its failing expectation via setupLegacyFn and only works because legacy and storage share one mock.

comentarios.texto: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers the failing Create expectation only through setupLegacyFn. It passes only because legacy and storage share one mock, so the storage Create gets that error by accident. Register the expectation in setupStorageFn and use separate mocks for legacy and storage, so the test really covers a storage failure.

issues.descricao: DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.

sugestoes.texto: BackupCode.tsx exports a component named `TwoFactor`, so React DevTools and error traces mislabel the backup-code input as the TOTP component. Rename the function to `BackupCode` to match the file and its intended identity.

Backup-code verification uses `indexOf` on the decrypted lower-case hex codes without normalizing the user input, so a capitalized entry fails even when correct. Lowercase `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')` before comparing, or normalize both sides.

The disable endpoint compares the supplied backup code to stored lower-case hex codes with case-sensitive `indexOf`, so uppercase input is rejected incorrectly. Normalize `req.body.backupCode` to lower case after stripping dashes.

`resetState` clears password and step but leaves `backupCodes` and the blob `backupCodesUrl` in memory when the modal closes, leaking a revocable object URL and stale recovery codes. Revoke the URL and reset the backup-code state in `resetState` and on unmount/Dialog close.

The backup-code branch assumes the password was already verified, but the preceding password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is truthy, so an attacker with a valid backup code can log in without the account password by supplying any `totpCode`. Verify the password inside the backup-code branch before consuming the code.

Backup-code consumption reads the decrypted JSON array, nulls one entry, and writes it back in a separate `prisma.user.update` with no row lock or transaction. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update lands, allowing the same backup code to authenticate more than once. Make the read-modify-write atomic, e.g., with a transaction or per-code rows guarded by a unique constraint.

issues.descricao: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

comentarios.texto: The new backup-code branch authenticates without guaranteeing the password check ran: password verification at line 121 is gated on `!credentials.totpCode`, and the branch at line 131 triggers on any truthy `credentials.backupCode` regardless of that gate. A POST to the credentials callback supplying a valid backup code together with any non-empty totpCode therefore takes the backup branch (skipping TOTP validation) while line 121 skips password verification — granting a session using only a second-factor backup code, with no account password. Require the password check before the backup branch, or include backupCode in the guard at line 121 (e.g. `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`).

The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

WHAT: The new backup-code login branch authenticates without verifying the password when credentials also contain any totpCode value (password check at line 121 is skipped when totpCode is truthy, and the backup branch never checks it). WHY: An attacker holding only a backup code can add a dummy totpCode to the credentials callback and log in without the password, reducing two factors to one. HOW: Verify the password whenever backupCode is used (or decouple the password check from totpCode presence).

issues.descricao: After enabling 2FA, onEnable is only called from the backup-codes Close button; dismissing the dialog by Escape/overlay never notifies the parent, so the settings page keeps showing 2FA disabled.

comentarios.texto: On a successful enable (response.status === 200) the modal no longer calls onEnable(); it only advances to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is now invoked solely from the 'close' button (line 269). If the user dismisses the Dialog via ESC or an overlay click, DialogContent's onOpenChange fires (wired to a plain setEnableModalOpen toggle at apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 and the conditional render at apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:36), so onEnable never runs. The parent callbacks (setEnableModalOpen(false) + utils.viewer.me.invalidate() / setEnabled(true)) are skipped, leaving the 2FA Switch unchecked and the UI showing 2FA as disabled even though the server has enabled it. Call onEnable() from the dismiss path (onOpenChange) or when transitioning into DisplayBackupCodes, not only from the Close button.

Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called and is only called from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog by Escape or overlay click (`onOpenChange`) while the codes are displayed, the parent is never notified that 2FA is enabled. The modal also keeps its step state and the plaintext backup codes. Call `onEnable` when 2FA is enabled, or make the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` on the DisplayBackupCodes step run the same handler as Close, which resets state and clears `backupCodes`.

issues.descricao: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, a copy-paste leftover from the TOTP component.
issues.textoGolden: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.

comentarios.texto: The default export is named `TwoFactor` but this file (BackupCode.tsx) renders the backup-code field and is imported as `BackupCode` by callers. The copied identifier misstates what the component is; rename the function to `BackupCode` so the name matches the file, the imports and the rendered content.

The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the name of the separate TOTP component. It is a copy-paste leftover and misleads readers and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` (`export default function TwoFactor`) while the file is BackupCode.tsx and it is imported as `BackupCode`. The name disagrees with the code's contract and duplicates the real TwoFactor component, misleading callers/readers. Rename to `BackupCode`.

issues.descricao: The backup-code copy e2e test only waits for the success toast, which is shown unconditionally, so it never verifies the clipboard content.

comentarios.texto: This 'copy' test does not verify the copy behaviour it names: it clicks backup-codes-copy and then only waits for the toast-success element. The handler (EnableTwoFactorModal) runs navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it and then calls showToast(...) unconditionally, so the toast appears even when the clipboard write is removed or fails. The assertion therefore passes with the backup-code copy feature broken; assert the actual effect (clipboard content, or that the formatted codes reached writeText) instead of the toast.

The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.
Copy test only waits for toast-success, explicitly TODOing clipboard check. Broken writeText (wrong format/empty) still passes; assert clipboard content equals formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can accept the same backup code more than once or overwrite each other's removal.
issues.textoGolden: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

comentarios.texto: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code is validated with indexOf (line 144) and only then persisted via prisma.user.update (line 149), with no unique constraint or lock. Two concurrent login requests sending the same valid backup code both read the unchanged row, both pass the indexOf check, and both obtain a session, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant. Consume the code atomically (e.g. a conditional update on the raw encrypted value / a dedicated used-backup-codes table with a unique index) so only one request can succeed.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, breaking the stated invariant that each backup code is single-use. Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code both read the same user.backupCodes array and both pass `index !== -1` before either `prisma.user.update` commits; both then persist a stale array (each nulling only its own index), so the code authenticates twice. Make consumption atomic (e.g. compare-and-swap on the encrypted value/updatedAt, a transaction with a conditional update, or an optimistic-locking retry) so exactly one request can claim a given code.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

issues.descricao: The copy button shows a success toast without awaiting clipboard.writeText, so a failed copy still tells the user their backup codes were saved.

comentarios.texto: The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

issues.descricao: The download e2e test checks only the filename, not that the file contains the displayed backup codes.

comentarios.texto: The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, explicitly TODOing file-content check. Empty/wrong backupCodes blob with correct filename still passes; assert downloaded file lines equal displayed/formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint's error log says 'backup code login' although it is disabling 2FA.
issues.textoGolden: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

comentarios.texto: The error log says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables two-factor authentication and does not log in. Change the message to describe disabling 2FA with a backup code.

issues.descricao: resetState does not clear backup codes/secret or revoke the backup-codes object URL, leaving a small blob URL leaked per setup cycle.
issues.textoGolden: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: resetState() clears only password/error/step and never clears backupCodes, secret, dataUri, nor revokes backupCodesUrl. WHY: Closing the modal after setup leaves TOTP secret and backup codes in memory and leaks the Blob object URL on every setup/close cycle. HOW: Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState and on unmount.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint calls replaceAll on req.body.backupCode without checking it is a string, so non-string input throws a 500.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll assumes a string with no type guard. WHY: A non-string JSON value (number/array) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of the 400 IncorrectBackupCode contract, breaking error handling and enabling error-probing. HOW: Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' (or String(...)) before replaceAll.

issues.descricao: Backup codes are matched case-sensitively against lowercase hex, so a user typing the code in uppercase is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

issues.descricao: The backup code is compared with the stored codes through Array.indexOf, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret backup codes.

sugestoes.texto: `fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` before checking that the setting is present, so a blank `embed_by_username` raises `NoMethodError` instead of gracefully skipping retrieval. Guard the setting with `.try(:downcase)` or a presence check before using it.

PollFeed imports arbitrary RSS/Atom item content as `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so `post.cooked` returns unsanitized feed HTML that is rendered with `raw` in the Discourse-origin embed iframe. A compromised feed can execute scripts and perform actions as the viewing Discourse user. Sanitize the feed HTML before import or avoid using `raw_html` for external content.

`perform_retrieve` runs the full `Jobs::PollFeed` job synchronously for every unknown embed URL, iterating over every RSS item without limit. This makes each new embed request O(feed size) and duplicates the hourly scheduled poll. Remove the synchronous full-feed poll from the retrieval path, or parse only until the requested URL is found.

The referer host check in `ensure_embeddable` compares hosts with case-sensitive string equality. A legitimate `Referer: http://EVILTROUT.com/` is rejected when `embeddable_host` is `eviltrout.com`, breaking embedding. Compare downcased hosts on both sides.

`invalid_host?` compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` case-sensitively. An embed URL such as `http://EVILTROUT.com/page` is treated as invalid even though hostnames are case-insensitive, causing retrieval to be skipped. Normalize both values with `downcase` before comparing.

issues.descricao: The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.textoGolden: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

comentarios.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.descricao: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.descricao: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.textoGolden: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.descricao: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.textoGolden: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

comentarios.texto: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

comentarios.texto: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.descricao: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

comentarios.texto: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.descricao: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

comentarios.texto: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.descricao: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

comentarios.texto: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.descricao: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.descricao: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

comentarios.texto: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.descricao: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

comentarios.texto: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.descricao: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

comentarios.texto: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.descricao: PollFeed.feed_key computes a per-feed cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-processed every hour without a modified-since check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the embed URL with open(url).read and no timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can block the background job and exhaust memory.
The retrieve throttle sets the Redis key with setnx and sets its TTL in a separate expire call, so a crash between the two leaves a key without expiry that blocks retrieval of that URL forever.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).

sugestoes.texto: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `flusher_processes=0` as `None`, falling back to one process per shard instead of honoring the configured limit. This lets an operator who passes zero unintentionally spawn as many flusher processes as there are partitions. Only fall back when `max_processes is None`, and validate or clamp zero to a sensible value.

The memory check loops over every flusher process's buffer and calls `get_memory_info()`, but every `SpansBuffer` uses the same Redis cluster via `get_redis_client()`, so `submit()` issues N redundant cluster INFO rounds. This multiplies Redis overhead by the number of flusher processes. Query cluster memory once from the parent and reuse the result instead of re-querying per buffer.

WHAT: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `flusher_processes=0` as unset. WHY: A user passing `--flusher-processes=0` expects 0 (or an error), but the flusher silently falls back to one process per Redis shard, using more resources than requested. HOW: Validate `max_processes` explicitly and reject or clamp values below 1 instead of relying on truthiness.

WHAT: The memory check calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` once per flusher process buffer. WHY: Every `SpansBuffer` uses `get_redis_client()` backed by the same Redis cluster (`settings.SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER`), so `INFO` is executed N times for the same nodes and results are summed redundantly. HOW: Query the cluster memory info once from a single buffer or the shared client, then reuse it for the threshold check.

issues.descricao: The wait_produce timer is tagged with 'shards' while sibling flusher metrics use 'shard' for the same value, so per-shard dashboards miss it.
issues.textoGolden: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

comentarios.texto: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with the key `"shards"`, while the other two metrics emitted in this same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` at line 185 and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` at line 195) use the key `"shard"`. All three carry the same `shard_tag` value, so this is a pure key-name disagreement: any dashboard or alert that groups/filters by the `shard` tag will silently receive no data from `wait_produce`. Rename the tag key to `"shard"` so all flusher metrics share one tag.

The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with key `shards` while every sibling metric introduced/updated in the same method (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) uses the singular key `shard`. Anything consuming this metric family by the `shard` tag (dashboards, alerts, tag-based aggregation) will silently receive no data for `wait_produce`, and per-shard breakdowns of produce latency will be incomplete. Change the tag to `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` so the tag contract matches the other flusher metrics.

The wait_produce timer tags with "shards", while the sibling metrics in the same loop use "shard" for the same value (shard_tag). Use one tag key, "shard", so queries and dashboards that group by it cover all of these metrics.

issues.descricao: The time.sleep(0.1) added to test_basic to let flusher threads process is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep.
issues.textoGolden: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The added synchronization point `time.sleep(0.1)` added after the second `step.poll()` is neutralized by the test's own `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 (same `time` module), so it does not actually wait. WHY: The comment says it 'Give[s] flusher threads time to process after drift change', but the call is a no-op, so the test still races the background flusher thread before `step.join()` and is liable to be flaky / to not exercise the intended post-drift flush path. HOW: Use a non-monkeypatched wait (e.g. capture the real sleep before patching, or use the flusher's thread/process join, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real timeout).

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait: line 15 of the same test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `sleep` on the global `time` module, so this call (and the flusher's own `time.sleep`) is a no-op. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is therefore false — the call returns instantly and provides no synchronisation, so the test does not actually wait for the flusher to process after the drift change. Either synchronise on a real condition (e.g. wait until the expected message is produced) or, if the original `time.sleep` is needed here, patch a module-scoped reference instead of the global `time.sleep`.

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so nothing waits for the flusher threads before `step.join()` and the `messages` assertion. Replace it with a condition-based wait, such as polling until `messages` is non-empty with a deadline. Use the real sleep saved before patching if a delay is needed.

issues.descricao: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
issues.textoGolden: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

comentarios.texto: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by self.mp_context.Process. When a worker hangs, the guard skips kill() and the replacement starts while the original worker remains alive, allowing overlapping flushing of the same shards if the original resumes and leaking hung workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process, and kill and join the old worker before replacing it.

The workers are created with get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances; these are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class). Consequently this guard skips kill() for actual production workers. When a worker hangs, the replacement starts while the original remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the spawn-context Process class for the check, and fix the identical check in join() so shutdown also terminates surviving workers.

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this guard skips kill() for production workers. When a live worker exceeds max-unhealthy-seconds, the code starts a replacement and overwrites its handle while the original is still running. If the original resumes, both workers flush the same shards, and repeated hangs can exceed the configured process limit. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or explicitly distinguish threads) and stop the old worker before replacing it.

issues.descricao: join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.
issues.textoGolden: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

comentarios.texto: join() breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier worker exhausts it, remaining flushers can continue running after shutdown or partition reassignment. Use the deadline only to limit waiting and still terminate and reap every remaining process.

Do not break out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires. If the first worker consumes the timeout, the next iteration breaks before terminating that worker or any subsequent workers. They may still be blocked in Redis or producer calls despite the shared stopped flag, leaving old workers running after strategy shutdown/reassignment. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of remaining time (using a type check that recognizes spawn-context workers).
join() waits for processes sequentially against a single shared deadline and breaks without terminating remaining processes once it expires, leaking them.

issues.descricao: The SpanFlusher docstring says it creates one process per shard, but shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

comentarios.texto: The docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the code at lines 60-66 shares shards across a capped number of processes (num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)); each shard assigned via i % self.num_processes). With the new --flusher-processes default of 1, a single process handles every shard, so the documented contract is the opposite of the behaviour this PR introduces (confirmed by test_flusher_processes_limit, which asserts 4 shards served by 2 processes). Update the docstring to say shards are distributed across up to max_processes flusher processes.

The new docstring says this creates one process per shard, but workers are capped by max_processes and shards are distributed among them. In particular, the CLI default of 1 means all assigned shards share one process. Describe capped workers with potentially multiple shards per worker so callers do not rely on per-shard process isolation.

The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but the number of processes is capped by max_processes (--flusher-processes), and shards are shared across processes via i % num_processes. Reword it to say that shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

issues.descricao: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.

comentarios.texto: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a falsy value as 'not provided'. The new `--flusher-processes` click option is `type=int`, so a user can pass `0`; that legitimate-but-falsy value is discarded and the flusher silently spawns one process per shard instead of honoring the requested limit. Use an explicit None check, e.g. `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (and validate/reject 0 upstream).

An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as an omitted limit by `or`, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` starts one process per assigned shard instead of respecting or rejecting the supplied zero limit. The CLI accepts zero as an integer and the factory forwards it unchanged. Default only when max_processes is None, and explicitly validate that supplied process limits are positive so zero cannot silently enable potentially many workers.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 is treated as 'unset' and silently expands to one process per shard. Use `max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and reject values below 1.

issues.descricao: A negative --flusher-processes value is not validated and makes SpanFlusher construction fail with KeyError.

comentarios.texto: `flusher_processes` is not validated to be >= 1. `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` lets a negative value through (it is truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty, leaving `process_to_shards_map` as `{}`. The following loop computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which for any negative divisor is 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError and the consumer fails to construct. Since `flusher_processes` is exposed as an int CLI option (`--flusher-processes`), a negative value is reachable from configuration. Guard with `max(1, self.num_processes)` / validate the input.
negative max_processes flows through `or` guard into min() -> empty map -> KeyError on i % num_processes; empty assigned_shards yields zero processes.

issues.descricao: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.

comentarios.texto: The new loop calls get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer even though SpansBuffer.get_memory_info delegates to iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client), which fetches INFO for the entire Redis cluster regardless of assigned_shards. With P flusher processes and memory backpressure enabled, each submitted batch now performs P identical cluster-wide memory queries on the consumer thread instead of one, increasing Redis traffic and blocking ingestion. Fetch cluster memory information once from a single buffer.
submit() loop calls buffer.get_memory_info() per flusher but each call is cluster-wide from same client, repeating identical INFO N× per submit.

issues.descricao: _create_process_for_shard is added but never called.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is newly added but has no caller anywhere (grep for `_create_process_for_shard(` finds only its definition); the restart path actually used is `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. WHY: This is dead code that indicates the intended per-shard restart wiring was left incomplete — any future caller relying on restarting only the process owning a given shard will silently do nothing, and it is confusing which restart path is authoritative. HOW: Remove `_create_process_for_shard`, or wire it into `_ensure_processes_alive` if per-shard restart was intended.

issues.descricao: test_flusher_processes_limit counts assigned shards instead of checking that each shard is assigned exactly once.

comentarios.texto: The assertion counts shard entries rather than verifying shard assignment. A broken distribution such as {0: [0, 1], 1: [0, 1]} still passes all assertions in this test while shards 2 and 3 are never flushed. Assert that the flattened mapping contains exactly the expected assigned shards, with no duplicates (and verify each worker's shard buffer uses that mapping), rather than only asserting a total of four.

sugestoes.texto: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for `scope: "team"`, but the internal zod schema still requires it and the constructor silently falls back to `this.options = null` when validation fails. A caller can pass `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` without a TypeScript error and receive `NOTHING_CONDITION` (no rows) instead of feedback that the options are invalid.
